prompts.character: REFRAMED 2026-08-29. The character agent addressed itself in the third person -- 'You are the decision process of {name}... Predict this character's next behavior' -- and its reasoning followed: 'Vessel is carrying... She needs to'. Measured over two agency_bench scenarios: removing every analyst word from the preamble changed the reasoning register NOT AT ALL, and rewriting the DECISION PROCEDURE and the numeric appraisal fields as questions a person can answer about themselves flipped it on both -- 'I am Vessel', with novelty and controllability reached introspectively instead of scored. The schema sets the register, not the preamble. DE-FICTIONALISED 2026-08-30, same reasoning carried one step further: the prompt opened 'You are {name}' and then spent forty-four phrases handing the frame back -- an author proposing things about you, your last attempt called a draft, a repeated line 'a stuck record on the page', a move that 'reads as' something to somebody, seven 'in character's, and nineteen sentences in which an engine records your clothing, caps your arousal, evicts your intentions and searches your memory. All of it now says the same thing without an actor outside the room, and the two Director sentences take the causality framing (an attempt whose success is not yours to decide) rather than a new agent's name. Field names are untouched -- `decision.authorial_offers` still says 'authorial', which needs an engine change, not a prompt one.
specialists.spatial.chunks.poses: CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-29. A pose detail was carrying another body's LOCATION ('holding her at the back of the mouth'), which is a claim `positions` owns -- so it went on saying it two rooms after that body was swallowed. The clause keeps a pose about the body it is stored under. `invalidate_moved_body_pose_details` is the deterministic floor under it, and only reaches the case where the detail NAMES the body.
card_person_note: ADDED 2026-08-30. No card prompt said what PERSON to write a field in, so generated cards came back third person throughout -- including the blocks that reach the character as its own mind, under a character prompt that had just been reframed to address it as itself. Measured on a live card: 258 third-person tokens against 30 second-person in the assembled payload, `psychology.self_model.summary` reading 'Mirelle sees herself as...', and `attire` carrying 'her forearms are smooth' into her own clothing line. This fragment splits the card by WHO READS EACH FIELD rather than by house style: first person for what only that mind reads (`psychology`, `knowledge.private_history`, `initial_state`), no person at all for what the Director, the narrator or an observer also reads (`embodiment`, `initial_outfit`, `competence.abilities`, `social.voice`, `knowledge.public_history`), and `identity.pronouns` untouched because it is a grammar fact about the world. Rewriting an EXISTING card's standing goals or belief/association claim text is a separate hazard and is not what this asks for: those strings are the fold keys `_merge_standing_intentions` and `_prune_seeded_psychology` dedupe on.

specialists.spatial.chunks.positions: CLAUSE ADDED 2026-08-30. The spatial specialist expresses where a small body has come to rest through `poses.support`, and only sometimes ALSO through `positions`; nothing said the second was the only channel that moves anyone. Measured across chat 101: `positions` carried the change on turns 61/63/81/83/87 and NOT on 65, 79 or 89, where a pose support named the destination room instead. So a body was recorded in the throat from turn 63 to turn 81 while every view described the stomach and then the small intestine -- eighteen turns of disagreement nobody saw, because the prose reads contacts and only movement reads positions. On turn 89 the beat that expelled her created the destination room, pointed her pose at it, removed every contact, and left `positions` empty: she stayed at the last interior station, her host could not see her, and her speech reached the room as 'A muffled voice'. LIMBS ARE NOT INTERIORS is in the clause because the room the Director built was a cupped palm carrying `parent_entity`, which every test the engine has reads as an INSIDE -- measured on the live scene, moving her to that palm leaves `containment_conceals` True, and only the host's own room clears it. SCOPED TO RELEASE DELIBERATELY: a deterministic trigger inferring the move from a room-valued pose support was designed and thrown away, because replayed against this chat it fires three times and two of them (turns 65 and 79) are transits DEEPER -- it would have ejected a swallowed body mid-passage. 'Released means out, and out is the room that character is standing in' is the one reading that cannot confuse the two directions. BOUNDED the same day, by the clause's own first live reroll. It fixed the release exactly as intended -- `positions: {"Hinami": "private_session_room"}`, no invented room -- and then also emitted `remove_rooms: ["Mirelle Sulmirath_rectum"]`, retiring a permanent station of that body's anatomy and rewiring the large intestine straight to the bedroom, so the card's six-station chain became five and every future passage would have skipped one. LIMBS ARE NOT INTERIORS read as licence to clear away the body-part room it had just emptied. The added sentence states the case the rest of the clause excludes: emptying a room is not removing it.
